decision.summary: The Jain governed proof boundary is pinned to and invokes the release-authoritative Jankurai 1.6.11 binary with SHA-256 fdb42e5f...014e. The interactive PATH binary also reports 1.6.11 but is a different, non-governed ELF and must not be substituted by version string alone.
decision.remaining_identity_risk: The direct split-host-ci release score lane resolves bare jankurai through the caller PATH and therefore selects the distinct .local build on this host. The installed governed proof boundary does not: it binds and executes the exact root-owned fdb42e5f build.

nested_redline_family.selection_note: redline-split-ops explicitly defaults JANKURAI_BIN to $HOME/.cargo/bin/jankurai; other Redline libraries include bare-command checks and must retain their owner-controlled PATH discipline until their own governed cutover.

jeryu_family.selection_note: The 1.6.10 Jeryu PR scripts intentionally prepend $HOME/.cargo/bin. A global replacement would break their explicit version checks; they require a reviewed family-wide render/cutover rather than a PATH mutation.

minimal_follow_up.action: Do not reinstall Jankurai and do not point the governed boundary at the .local binary. The required fdb42e5f build is already installed, receipt-bound, root-copied, and config-bound.

The jain-split-ops owner should decide whether the direct split-host-ci release score lane must also bind an exact Jankurai digest instead of relying on a version-only PATH lookup. This audit made no source or config change.
Do not mechanically bump Jeryu or Redline 1.6.10 pins. Their owners must perform their existing governed family cutovers with exact binary identity and receipts.
